 US Attorney: Louisiana woman sent fake check to IRS, made $17 million in refund claims 
 BY BRIAN McCALLUM | Staff writer 
 Brian McCallum

 A Boyce woman was convicted Tuesday by a federal jury in the Western District of Louisiana of several charges related to tax refund fraud, and prosecutors said she sent a fake check to the IRS.
 Jane Frances Pierce, 64, was found by a jury to be involved in $17 million in fraudulent claims. She was found guilty of mail fraud, filing false tax returns, money laundering and corruptly interfering with an IRS investigation.
 According to information from the office of U.S. Attorney Zach Keller, she filed fraudulent claims for more than $10 million in refunds for a trust she controlled and for $7 million in refunds for an estate she controlled.

 BY BRIAN McCALLUM | Staff writer

 Prosecutors claimed that, after she received $1 million from the IRS, she used the money for personal benefit, including buying a house and paying for family members’ mortgages. She later filed a false amended tax return, filed a false court document and sent a fake check to the IRS.
 Pierce will be sentenced Feb. 16 and faces up to 20 years for mail fraud, 10 for money laundering and three years each for filing a false tax return and investigation interference.
 “Tax fraudsters steal not just from the United States government but also from every person who works hard, pays their taxes, and trusts that everyone else is doing the same,” Keller said.
